metadata.title: How Many Days' Wages Would Cover the Basics?
metadata.description:
Bread, fuel, soap and light: how many days of a London labourer's pay did a reconstructed annual basket of basic needs cost?

This film follows selected London labourer estimates from before the Black Death through 1850–1899. The basket is a working reconstruction for a family of four, not a record of every household's spending or a comparison with today. Wage-days are a way to compare the basket with daily pay; they do not tell us how many days any individual actually worked.

The answer does not move steadily in one direction. The basket takes about 176 wage-days in the first half of the 1500s, rises to about 216 in 1600–1649, then falls to about 116 in the second half of the 1800s. The reversal shows why a larger daily wage alone cannot tell us what necessities cost relative to pay.

#CostOfLiving #Wages #EconomicHistory #PaperDetour
